label: Amalekites Genocide
description: God's Old Testament injunction to Moses that too many Amalekite children were spared — Hitchens's exhibit of divinely-commanded atrocity, not equivalent to a hard medical decision.
name: amalekites-genocide

label: Andromeda Collision
description: The Andromeda galaxy on a direct collision course — Hitchens's exhibit for capricious or absent design.
name: andromeda-collision

label: Atonement
description: Christ's sacrifice is retroactive to everyone before him, so God 'always had a witness' (creation, conscience, Christ).
name: atonement

label: Big Bang
description: The accepted origin of the universe; Turek accepts it and infers a 'banger'.
name: big-bang

label: Borrowing From Theism
description: Turek's charge: Hitchens must 'sit in God's lap to slap his face'.
name: borrowing-from-theism

label: Burden Of Proof
description: Who must establish the claim; both accept a share.
name: burden-of-proof

label: Celestial Dictatorship
description: Theism framed as totalitarian, master-slave submission — the oldest enemy of our moral autonomy.
name: celestial-dictatorship

label: Choice Argument
description: Turek's claim that moving from non-existence to existence requires a choice, and only persons choose.
name: choice-argument

label: Conscience
description: Innate moral sense (Socrates's daemon, Smith's internal witness).
name: conscience

label: Consciousness
description: Subjective experience Turek says chemicals cannot explain.
name: consciousness

label: Contraception
description: Hitchens calls it nonsensical and immoral for the Church to equate contraception with abortion; cites the ectopic pregnancy as a humanist no-starter.
name: contraception

label: Determinism
description: Physical law fixes all events (Einstein, Provine's Darwinism); Turek says it undercuts trust in reasoning.
name: determinism

label: Divine Command
description: The divine-command standard: right and wrong fixed by God's nature and command.
name: divine-command

label: Divine Permission
description: Felt divine authorization Hitchens links to atrocity.
name: divine-permission

label: Empathy
description: Biologically grounded basis for morality raised in audience Q&A.
name: empathy

label: Enlightenment Values
description: The post-religious values Turek says Hitchens wants all to adopt — which Turek reframes as 'the dictatorship of Christopher Hitchens'.
name: enlightenment-values

label: Eschatology
description: End-times doctrine; the rapture, Armageddon, the apocalypse, a 'cult of death' set against a promised new Heaven and new earth.
name: eschatology

label: Event Horizon
description: Hawking's 'lip of the black hole'; Hitchens uses it to show our God-talk is the vocabulary of our infancy.
name: event-horizon

label: Fine-Tuning
description: Constants on a razor's edge permitting life.
name: fine-tuning

label: Free Will
description: Genuine choice Turek says materialism cannot supply.
name: free-will

label: Good Samaritan
description: The Samaritan helped without religious instruction and predates Christianity — morality 'written on your heart'.
name: good-samaritan

label: Heat Death
description: The far-future maximal-entropy state; used by both (Turek vs eternity, Hitchens for poor design).
name: heat-death

label: Hume On Miracles
description: Error is always likelier than a suspension of nature in one's favor.
name: hume-on-miracles

label: Irreducible Complexity
description: Raised in audience Q&A: whether such biological structures could have formed by chance.
name: irreducible-complexity

label: Is-Ought Problem
description: Hume's bar on deriving an 'ought' from an 'is'.
name: is-ought-problem

label: Materialism
description: Only matter exists; Turek's target across the four supporting arguments.
name: materialism

label: Mind-Forged Manacles
description: Blake's phrase for self-imposed religious tyranny (limbo, hell).
name: mind-forged-manacles

label: Miracle
description: A suspension of natural order (the regular course of nature), per Hume.
name: miracle

label: Moral Lawgiver
description: The prescriber Turek infers from the prescription of morality.
name: moral-lawgiver

label: Naturalism
description: Natural causes suffice to explain the world; every origin question now has a natural or sufficient explanation.
name: naturalism

label: Non-Overlapping Magisteria
description: Gould's thesis that science and religion address separate domains.
name: non-overlapping-magisteria

label: Objective Moral Values
description: Mind-independent moral facts at the center of the moral exchange.
name: objective-moral-values

label: Occam's Razor
description: Dispose of needless assumptions — Hitchens removes the prime mover.
name: occam's-razor

label: Ontological Argument
description: To conceive a thing is for it to be 'real in the mind' (parodied via limbo).
name: ontological-argument

label: Optimal Design
description: Turek's closing: design need not be optimal; you can't call it suboptimal without knowing the designer's purpose (vs. Gould's panda's thumb).
name: optimal-design

label: Original Sin
description: 'We were well in the beginning but then we messed up'; the Fall, which Hitchens parodies as 'created sick, commanded to be well'.
name: original-sin

label: Panspermia
description: Crick/Hoyle's seeded-life proposal; Turek calls it a backhanded concession.
name: panspermia

label: Parable Of The Talents
description: Turek's counter that Jesus did not simply preach 'take no thought for tomorrow'.
name: parable-of-the-talents

label: Prime Mover
description: The first-cause designer Hitchens applies Occam's razor to remove — 'we don't need the prime mover at all'.
name: prime-mover

label: Probability Argument
description: Turek's cross-examination framing: not a proof of God but a cumulative case that God is the more probable explanation.
name: probability-argument

label: Problem Of Evil
description: Implicit in 'created sick, commanded to be well' — suffering counts against a good designer.
name: problem-of-evil

label: Resurrection
description: Hitchens notes it was 'commonplace' in the gospels.
name: resurrection

label: Scapegoating
description: Casting sins onto a substitute; called primitive and barbaric.
name: scapegoating

label: Singularity
description: The point reversed expansion collapses to; Turek equates it with 'nothing'.
name: singularity

label: Solipsism
description: Religion's appeal to self-regard — wanting to be objects of a divine plan — likened to a quick peek at one's horoscope.
name: solipsism

label: Specified Complexity
description: Information in living systems Turek says only minds produce.
name: specified-complexity

label: Suicide Bombing
description: Wickedness Hitchens says is characteristically religious, alongside genital mutilation and circumcision dictated 'in God's name'.
name: suicide-bombing

label: Termination Of Pregnancy
description: The abortion exchange: Turek presses Hitchens's book on the unborn child / fetus; embryology and early viability are invoked.
name: termination-of-pregnancy

label: Theocracy
description: Hitchens's post-9/11 cause: opposing theocracy and its messianic, end-times depredations internationally.
name: theocracy

label: Vicarious Redemption
description: Salvation by another's suffering through human sacrifice; Hitchens's central moral objection.
name: vicarious-redemption

label: Virgin Birth
description: Parthenogenesis: a miracle a design argument can never reach, even if a male-free pregnancy could be tracked.
name: virgin-birth

label: Watchmaker
description: Paley's image: design implies a designer.
name: watchmaker
